strings.name: Madonna
strings.summary: Madonna moved from dance training and New York clubs into international pop, repeatedly reshaping her public image through songs, videos and tours. Collaborating with different producers, she explored dance and electronic music while working in film and business. Her treatment of religion, sexuality and gender attracted both acclaim and controversy, making creative autonomy central to her cultural influence.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected chronology extends to 2026-07-03. This is not a complete catalogue of works or appearances; later plans are not treated as completed events.
strings.influence.rationale: Her music, dance and visual reinvention changed popular culture and influenced women’s creative autonomy and public expressions of gender.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Pop across media
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Connected records, dance, music videos and large tours while repeatedly changing her performance style.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Creative and business autonomy
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Participated in writing, production and Maverick; expressions concerning religion and gender brought both support and controversy.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Released Confessions II
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Issued a new album with Stuart Price, continuing her work in dance music.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Closed her tour in Rio
strings.timeline.event-2.text: A free Copacabana Beach concert concluded the Celebration Tour.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Entered the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Her sustained musical and performance influence was honored.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Released Confessions on a Dance Floor
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Continuous dance sequencing developed her electronic-pop approach.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Released Ray of Light
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Worked with William Orbit and others to explore electronic music and personal experience.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Starred in Evita
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Led the musical film and received a Golden Globe the following year.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Co-founded Maverick
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Established an entertainment business with partners, extending her music and commercial activities.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Released Like a Prayer
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Music and imagery addressed religion and identity, prompting wide debate.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Released Like a Virgin
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Her second album expanded her international recognition.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Released her debut album
strings.timeline.event-10.text: The self-titled record established her as a dance-pop singer.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Moved to New York
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Left university dance studies to seek performance opportunities in New York.
strings.timeline.event-12.title: Born in Michigan
strings.timeline.event-12.text: Born Madonna Louise Ciccone; received dance training as a child.
